自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a mass in her left breast. A diagnosis of breast cancer is made and a mastectomy is planned. During the procedure, involvement of the muscle deep to the fatty tissue is seen and a radical mastectomy with removal of the breast, underlying chest muscles, and lymph nodes is performed. Removal of this muscle will most likely compromise which of the following functions?

options.text: Abduction of the humerus at the shoulder
Adduction of the humerus at the shoulder
External rotation of the humerus at the shoulder

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The muscle deep to the breast is the pectoralis major. Removing it weakens adduction and internal rotation of the humerus, so B is correct. A is primarily performed by the deltoid after the first 15 degrees, with the supraspinatus initiating abduction. C is produced mainly by the infraspinatus and teres minor. D is performed by the trapezius and rhomboids. E is performed by the biceps brachii and supinator. The clue is the muscle removed in a radical mastectomy, not the breast tissue itself.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: deltoid produces most shoulder abduction; supraspinatus initiates it.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: pectoralis major adducts and internally rotates the humerus.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: infraspinatus and teres minor are the principal external rotators.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: trapezius and rhomboids retract the scapula.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: biceps brachii and supinator supinate the forearm.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The pectoralis major contributes to humeral adduction; compare shoulder movements with the rotator-cuff actions and arm-movement diagrams.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 59-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious by his wife. On examination, he is unable to move his extremities and has decerebrate posturing. The patient is unable to speak or move his face. He is able to answer yes/no questions by using eye blinks or vertical eye movements, but has no horizontal eye movements. He is unable to move his limbs in response to commands and has upgoing plantar responses bilaterally. Pathology of the following vessels is most likely responsible for this patient's condition?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is locked-in syndrome from a ventral pontine lesion: corticospinal and corticobulbar pathways are damaged, causing quadriplegia and loss of voluntary facial and speech movements, while vertical eye movements and blinking are preserved. Bilateral long-tract findings localize to the pons supplied by the basilar artery. AICA and PICA infarcts usually cause lateral pontine and lateral medullary syndromes, respectively; a middle cerebral artery infarct causes a hemispheric pattern; vertebral artery occlusion more typically causes lateral medullary findings. The patient's preserved awareness with loss of horizontal gaze is the key localization clue.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: AICA occlusion usually causes lateral pontine findings such as ipsilateral facial paralysis, vertigo, or hearing loss.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: basilar artery occlusion can injure the ventral pons bilaterally and produce locked-in syndrome.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: MCA occlusion produces a unilateral hemispheric syndrome, often with contralateral face/arm deficits and cortical signs.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: PICA occlusion classically causes lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: vertebral artery occlusion more often produces lateral medullary findings than a bilateral ventral pontine syndrome.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Basilar artery occlusion can injure pontine corticospinal/corticobulbar tracts, causing quadriplegia and loss of voluntary facial, mouth, and tongue movement; vertical eye movements may remain intact in locked-in syndrome.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 21-year-old man is bitten by a stray cat. The wound becomes erythematous and swollen despite appropriate wound care. Five days later, the patient notices a pustule at the wound site that was not previously present and develops a low-grade fever. His symptoms persist, and two weeks later, he complains of pain in the back of his leg. Physical examination reveals a swollen tender lymph node in the popliteal fossa. An infected cat bite in which of the following sites would most likely induce lymphadenopathy in this region?

options.text: Lateral side of the dorsum of the foot
Medial side of the leg below the knee
Medial side of the sole of the foot

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The lateral part of the dorsum of the foot drains with the small saphenous vein to popliteal lymph nodes, so A is correct. Most superficial lymph from the lower limb follows the great saphenous vein to superficial inguinal nodes. The medial leg, medial sole, and thigh therefore drain mainly to inguinal nodes rather than the popliteal fossa. The cat bite with a primary skin lesion followed by regional tender lymphadenopathy is consistent with cat-scratch disease, but the question asks specifically which drainage territory reaches the popliteal nodes.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: lymph from the lateral dorsum of the foot accompanies the small saphenous vein to popliteal nodes.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the lateral thigh drains primarily to superficial inguinal nodes.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: the medial leg follows the great saphenous pathway to superficial inguinal nodes.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the medial sole generally joins the great saphenous/superficial inguinal drainage pathway.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the thigh drains to superficial inguinal nodes, not the popliteal group.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid 2026 does not directly cover the superficial lymphatic drainage route tested here; no unrelated page number is assigned.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 50-year-old man who is an electrician comes to the physician because of recent onset pain and tingling in his left arm. Neurologic examination shows absence of sensation to light touch and pinprick on the fourth and fifth digits of his left hand and his medial forearm. There is also clawing of all digits of the left hand. Rotating the patient's head to the left side with the neck extended results in loss of the radial pulse on the left. An x-ray of the neck shows a cervical rib. Which of the following structures is most likely being compressed?

options.text: C6 root of the brachial plexus
Lower trunk of the brachial plexus
Medial cord of the brachial plexus
Upper trunk of the brachial plexus

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is thoracic outlet syndrome caused by compression near a cervical rib. The sensory loss in the medial forearm and ulnar digits, together with clawing of the hand, localizes to C8–T1 fibers in the lower trunk of the brachial plexus; positional loss of the radial pulse indicates associated subclavian vessel compression. A C6 root or upper-trunk lesion produces a more proximal C5–C6 pattern. The long thoracic nerve lesion causes serratus anterior weakness and winged scapula. A medial-cord lesion is more distal than the classic lower-trunk compression at the thoracic outlet, while an isolated ulnar nerve lesion would not explain medial-forearm sensory loss or the vascular finding.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: C6 root injury would affect a C6 distribution and would not explain the cervical-rib thoracic-outlet pattern.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: long thoracic nerve injury weakens serratus anterior, causing winged scapula, not medial-hand sensory loss.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: the lower trunk (C8–T1) is compressed in thoracic outlet syndrome associated with a cervical rib.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the medial cord contains lower-trunk fibers but is distal to the typical thoracic-outlet compression site.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: ulnar neuropathy can affect ulnar digits but not medial forearm sensation or the radial pulse.
choice_explanations.F: Incorrect: upper-trunk (C5–C6) injury causes an Erb-pattern deficit, not C8–T1 clawing.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Thoracic outlet compression can affect the lower brachial-plexus trunk (C8–T1); a cervical/anomalous first rib is a recognized cause.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of several stab wounds he sustained in a gang fight. Physical examination shows a 3-cm penetrating wound on the posterolateral aspect of the neck that has partially severed the C6 ventral ramus as it emerges through the scalene interval. The patient reports pain in the region of the wound, and there is significant bruising in this area. Which of the following additional findings will most likely be seen in this patient?

options.text: Anesthesia in skin covering the hypothenar eminence
Weakness in the ability to protract the scapula

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The long thoracic nerve receives fibers directly from the ventral rami of C5–C7. A partial C6 ventral-ramus injury can therefore weaken the serratus anterior, impair scapular protraction, and cause winging of the scapula. Hypothenar sensory loss and thenar atrophy arise from distal ulnar or median nerve lesions; hoarseness suggests vagal/recurrent laryngeal nerve dysfunction; thumb-flexion weakness points to median-innervated flexors rather than the long thoracic nerve.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: hypothenar skin sensation is supplied by the ulnar nerve, not the long thoracic nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: hoarseness suggests vagus/recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: thenar atrophy suggests median nerve/recurrent branch injury.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: long thoracic nerve fibers arise from C5–C7 ventral rami and supply serratus anterior, which protracts and stabilizes the scapula.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: thumb flexion depends on median-innervated muscles, not serratus anterior.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The long thoracic nerve arises from C5–C7 ventral rami and innervates serratus anterior; injury can cause winged scapula and impaired scapular stabilization.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension is admitted to the intensive care unit after sustaining a stroke. He describes recent onset dizziness and difficulty standing upright without falling over. Physical examination shows loss of pain and temperature sensation on the right side of the face and the left side of the body. The right eye exhibits partial ptosis and pupillary miosis. He is discharged 6 days later and is transferred to a rehabilitation center. A more comprehensive physical examination also reveals difficulty in elevating the tongue to the roof of the mouth. Dysfunction of which of the following muscles is most likely responsible for this finding?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The crossed face/body pain-temperature loss, ipsilateral Horner syndrome, dizziness, and ataxia indicate lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome, usually due to PICA or vertebral artery infarction. The nucleus ambiguus and vagal fibers may be involved. Palatoglossus is the only tongue muscle innervated by the vagus nerve (CN X); the other intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles are supplied by CN XII. This explains impaired elevation of the posterior tongue/palatal arch.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: buccinator is a facial-expression muscle supplied by CN VII; it compresses the cheek.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: geniohyoid is supplied by C1 fibers traveling with CN XII and helps move the hyoid/anterior floor of the mouth.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: palatoglossus is innervated by CN X via the pharyngeal plexus and can be affected with nucleus ambiguus involvement.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: palatopharyngeus is vagus-innervated, but it elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing rather than elevating the tongue.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: tensor veli palatini is supplied by V3 and tenses the soft palate.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Lateral medullary syndrome can damage nucleus ambiguus pathways; CN IX/X involvement causes dysphagia and related palatal/pharyngeal deficits.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 24-year-old man who is a truck driver is brought to the emergency department because of a fracture of the right humerus. Physical examination shows an inability to extend the right hand at the wrist. The patient can flex all of the fingers but cannot make a tight fist with the right hand. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured as a result of this fracture?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: A humeral shaft fracture can injure the radial nerve in the spiral groove, producing wrist drop from loss of wrist extension. Finger flexors may remain intact, but grip is weakened because the wrist cannot be held extended to place the long finger flexors at an effective length. The fracture level and wrist-extension deficit are the key clues.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: axillary nerve injury causes deltoid weakness and sensory loss over the lateral shoulder, usually after a surgical-neck fracture.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the medial brachial cutaneous nerve is sensory and does not control wrist extension.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: median nerve injury weakens forearm pronation, thenar function, or selected finger flexion, not wrist extension as the main finding.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: musculocutaneous nerve injury weakens elbow flexion and forearm supination.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: radial nerve injury at the humeral shaft causes wrist drop and weak grip.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: A midshaft humerus fracture can injure the radial nerve and cause wrist drop; loss of wrist extension also reduces grip strength.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 56-year-old man with a history of chronic hypertension comes to the physician because of recent onset palpitations. He says that he particularly notices the palpitations when he lacks sleep or drinks too much caffeine. Physical examination shows a heart rhythm that is irregularly irregular but there is no evidence of murmurs or gallops. ECG reveals absent P waves. The patient is started on a beta blocker. Three months later, he arrives in the emergency department after acute onset weakness and lethargy. CT scan reveals no hemorrhage but diffusion-weighted MRI reveals evidence of ischemic stroke. Absent blood flow to which of the following arteries is most likely to produce the greatest amount of ischemic damage?

options.text: Anterior cerebral artery at its origin from the internal carotid artery
Middle cerebral artery at its origin from the internal carotid artery
Posterior cerebral artery at its origin from the basilar artery

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The middle cerebral artery is not part of the Circle of Willis, so there is no direct Circle-of-Willis route to compensate for its occlusion. It supplies much of the lateral cerebral hemisphere; proximal MCA occlusion can therefore produce a large ischemic territory. The ACA and PCA are connected to the circle, and the anterior and posterior communicating arteries are themselves collateral links.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: ACA is part of the anterior cerebral circulation and communicates with the opposite side through the anterior communicating artery.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the anterior communicating artery is a collateral connection between the two anterior cerebral arteries.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: MCA is not part of the Circle of Willis and supplies a large lateral cerebral territory.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: PCA is part of the posterior circulation and connects to the Circle of Willis through the posterior communicating artery.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the posterior communicating artery is a collateral link between the internal carotid and posterior cerebral circulations.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The Circle of Willis provides collateral routes between anterior and posterior cerebral circulations; the middle cerebral artery is outside the ring and supplies the lateral hemisphere.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks' gestation comes to the physician because of pain and tingling in her hands. She also says that at times her hands feel numb; however, she cannot pinpoint exactly where the numbness is centered. She reports no issues with her pregnancy. Physical examination shows wasting of the thenar eminence. Physical examination will most likely also reveal loss of sensation in which of the following sites?

options.text: Dorsal aspect of the hand (not fingers) on the medial side
Dorsal aspect of the hand (not fingers) on the lateral side
Dorsal aspect of the proximal part of the forefinger
Dorsal aspect of the proximal part of the thumb
Nail bed of the third digit

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Pregnancy-related fluid retention can precipitate carpal tunnel syndrome by compressing the median nerve beneath the flexor retinaculum. Thenar wasting indicates median motor involvement. The median nerve supplies the palmar lateral 3½ digits and the distal dorsal tips/nail beds of those digits, including the third digit, so E is correct. The palmar cutaneous branch leaves proximal to the tunnel and supplies thenar skin, so sensation over the thenar eminence is usually spared. Dorsal hand skin proximal to the fingertips is supplied mainly by the radial or ulnar nerves.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the medial/dorsal hand is primarily supplied by the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the lateral dorsal hand proximal to the fingertips is supplied mainly by the superficial radial nerve.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: proximal dorsal finger skin is supplied primarily by radial/ulnar dorsal branches; median nerve sensory loss is prominent at the distal fingertips/nail beds.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: proximal dorsal thumb skin is mainly supplied by the superficial radial nerve.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the median nerve supplies the distal dorsal tips and nail beds of the lateral 3½ digits, including digit 3.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Median nerve compression in carpal tunnel syndrome causes thenar weakness/atrophy and sensory symptoms in the lateral digits; the palmar cutaneous branch travels outside the tunnel, sparing thenar skin sensation.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a severe sore throat. She describes significant pain with swallowing and general feelings of malaise. Her parents report that the patient has had a high fever for the past several days. Physical examination shows an erythematous patch on the upper posterior pharynx and tenderness of the cervical lymph nodes. Her temperature is 39.5°C (103.1°F). The nerve responsible for this patient's throat pain is also involved in which of the following functions?

options.text: Sensory input from carotid sinus baroreceptors
Taste in the anterior 2/3 of the tongue

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Pain from the posterior pharynx is carried by the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX). CN IX also carries afferent sensory information from the carotid sinus baroreceptors to the nucleus tractus solitarius, so D is correct. Head rotation is performed by sternocleidomastoid (CN XI); intrinsic tongue muscles are supplied by CN XII; lower-jaw sensation is carried by V3; and taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by CN VII via the chorda tympani.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: sternocleidomastoid, innervated by CN XI, rotates the head to the opposite side.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: CN XII supplies the intrinsic tongue muscles, except palatoglossus.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: sensory innervation of the lower jaw is carried by the mandibular division of CN V.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: CN IX carries carotid sinus baroreceptor afferents and sensation from the posterior pharynx.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by CN VII through the chorda tympani.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Carotid sinus baroreceptor afferents travel in CN IX to the nucleus tractus solitarius; aortic arch afferents travel in CN X.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a headache that began several days ago and has become progressively worse. A single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) image using technetium (Tc)-labeled red blood cells is shown. Greater blood flow is indicated by orange to red colors and poor blood flow is indicated by blue or lack of signal. Which of the following structures shows an abnormal blood perfusion pattern according to this imaging study?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The image shows markedly reduced signal in the right transverse sinus compared with the left, indicating abnormal flow in that dural venous sinus. The transverse sinuses carry blood from the confluence of sinuses toward the sigmoid sinuses, which continue as the internal jugular veins. The asymmetry, rather than a focal cerebral arterial territory, identifies the transverse sinus.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the inferior sagittal sinus lies along the free inferior edge of the falx and is not the asymmetric lateral channel shown.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the internal jugular veins are downstream after the sigmoid sinuses and lie outside the cranial image field.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: the middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral cerebral hemisphere; this is not a cortical arterial perfusion defect.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the posterior cerebral artery supplies occipital and inferomedial temporal cortex, not a dural venous channel.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the superior sagittal sinus is a midline channel; the abnormality is in one lateral transverse sinus.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: one transverse sinus has markedly reduced tracer signal, consistent with impaired flow.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Cerebral veins drain into dural venous sinuses, which ultimately empty into the internal jugular veins. The superior sagittal, straight, and occipital sinuses drain toward the confluence; paired transverse sinuses run laterally to the sigmoid sinuses. The First Aid index also links venous sinus thrombosis with factor V Leiden.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination because of increasing pain in her right eye. She was recently diagnosed with severe optic neuritis in her right eye. Her past neurologic history is significant for weakness in her right leg 2 years ago that resolved spontaneously. She also reports tingling in her left hand 5 years ago, which resolved without treatment. The physician tests her pupillary response by shining a light in each eye. Which of the following findings is most likely?

options.text: Light in right: both pupils constrict. Light in left: neither pupil responds.
Light in right: right pupil constricts, left does not. Light in left: both pupils constrict.
Light in right: right pupil constricts, left does not. Light in left: only the right pupil constricts.
Light in right: right pupil does not respond, left constricts. Light in left: both pupils constrict.
Light in right: right pupil does not respond, left constricts. Light in left: right pupil does not respond, left constricts.
Light in right: neither pupil responds. Light in left: both pupils constrict.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Recurrent neurologic deficits separated in time and affecting different locations, together with optic neuritis, strongly suggest multiple sclerosis. The right optic nerve is the afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex. Shining light in the affected right eye produces no afferent signal, so neither pupil constricts. Shining light in the unaffected left eye sends afferent input to both Edinger–Westphal nuclei, so both pupils constrict. This is a right relative afferent pupillary defect.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: if the right optic nerve is affected, light in the right eye cannot trigger either pupil; light in the healthy left eye should trigger both.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: this describes a normal right-eye afferent response, which is inconsistent with right optic neuritis.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: an intact left optic nerve should drive bilateral constriction when illuminated.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the left pupil constricts when the right eye is illuminated, showing that afferent input from the right eye reaches the brain; that does not fit a complete right optic-nerve block.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: this pattern suggests an efferent defect affecting the right pupil, not a right optic-nerve afferent lesion.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: a right optic-nerve afferent defect prevents either pupil responding to right-eye illumination, while left-eye illumination activates both efferent limbs.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Multiple sclerosis causes CNS demyelination with neurologic deficits separated in time and space; optic neuritis is a common presentation. A unilateral optic-nerve lesion causes an afferent pupillary defect: illumination of the affected eye fails to constrict either pupil, while illumination of the unaffected eye constricts both.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 26-year-old woman has worked out twice a week for several months at a local exercise club. Recently, she developed severe weakness in abduction of her thighs against resistance using an exercise machine. It is determined that this weakness began soon after she received an intramuscular injection of a vaccine. Damage to which of the following nerves is most likely responsible for this loss of function?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Hip abduction is chiefly produced by gluteus medius and minimus, with help from tensor fasciae latae. These muscles are supplied by the superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1). An intramuscular injection placed too high and medially in the gluteal region can injure this nerve, weakening the abductors and potentially causing a Trendelenburg gait. The clue is loss of hip abduction after an injection, not foot or knee weakness.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the deep fibular nerve supplies anterior-compartment leg muscles for ankle dorsiflexion and toe extension; injury may cause foot drop.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the femoral nerve supplies the anterior thigh, especially quadriceps for knee extension, and contributes to hip flexion.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: the obturator nerve supplies medial-thigh adductors; injury weakens hip adduction, not abduction.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: the superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius and minimus, the primary hip abductors.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the tibial nerve supplies posterior leg and plantar-foot muscles; injury impairs plantarflexion and toe flexion.

A.summary: The deep fibular nerve supplies tibialis anterior and other anterior-compartment muscles; loss of dorsiflexion can produce foot drop.

B.summary: The femoral nerve supplies the anterior thigh; quadriceps weakness impairs knee extension, and hip flexion may also weaken.

C.summary: The obturator nerve supplies medial-thigh muscles, including hip adductors; a lesion causes weakness of adduction.

D.summary: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1) supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, and tensor fasciae latae. Injury can follow an improperly placed gluteal injection and causes Trendelenburg gait from impaired pelvic stabilization.

E.summary: The tibial nerve supplies posterior-compartment leg and plantar-foot muscles; a proximal lesion weakens plantarflexion and toe flexion.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid lists gluteus medius/minimus as hip abductors (p. 455) and identifies their superior gluteal nerve supply, injection injury, and Trendelenburg gait (p. 456).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 33-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a skiing accident. She was going too fast and grabbed a tree with her right arm to avoid colliding with another skier. Since the injury, she has weakness and numbness in her right upper extremity. Examination shows pain and numbness in the medial two fingers, the medial aspect of the palm, and the medial aspect of the arm and forearm on the right. She also has clawing of digits IV-V of the right hand. Which structure is most likely injured?

options.text: Lower trunk of the brachial plexus
Upper trunk of the brachial plexus

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Traction on an abducted arm can injure the lower trunk (C8-T1) of the brachial plexus, producing Klumpke palsy. C8-T1 fibers contribute to intrinsic hand muscles and the ulnar side of the hand; lower-trunk injury can therefore cause clawing and sensory loss along the medial hand, forearm, and arm. This is broader than an isolated ulnar neuropathy because the medial forearm sensation is also affected.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor; injury causes impaired shoulder abduction and sensory loss over the lateral shoulder.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: lower-trunk (C8-T1) injury causes Klumpke palsy with intrinsic hand weakness/clawing and medial sensory deficits.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: an isolated median lesion causes median-distribution sensory/motor findings, not medial forearm sensory loss and ulnar-sided clawing.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: radial neuropathy chiefly impairs wrist/finger extension and can cause wrist drop with dorsolateral hand sensory loss.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: ulnar neuropathy can claw digits IV-V, but does not explain sensory loss over the medial forearm and arm.
choice_explanations.F: Incorrect: upper-trunk (C5-C6) injury produces Erb palsy, with shoulder abduction/external rotation and elbow-flexion weakness.

A.summary: The axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor; injury near the surgical neck of the humerus causes weak abduction and lateral-shoulder sensory loss.

B.summary: Lower-trunk C8-T1 injury (Klumpke palsy) weakens intrinsic hand muscles and causes ulnar-sided hand/forearm sensory loss; T1 involvement can produce Horner syndrome.

C.summary: Median nerve injury affects thenar muscles and sensation in the lateral 3½ digits; the palmar cutaneous branch remains outside the carpal tunnel.

D.summary: Radial nerve injury can cause wrist drop and sensory loss over the dorsolateral hand, depending on lesion level.

E.summary: Ulnar nerve injury weakens intrinsic hand muscles and causes sensory loss on the medial hand; it does not account for medial-forearm sensory loss.

F.summary: Upper-trunk C5-C6 injury (Erb palsy) affects shoulder and elbow functions, classically producing the waiter-tip posture.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's brachial plexus diagram and lesion table contrast upper-trunk Erb palsy with lower-trunk Klumpke palsy; the C8-T1 pattern matches the medial sensory loss and hand clawing here.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 16-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department after sustaining multiple knife wounds, including one to the axilla. Neurologic examination suggests an injury to the posterior cord of the brachial plexus. Which of the following muscles is most likely to be paralyzed?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The posterior cord gives rise to the axillary and radial nerves. Of the listed muscles, the deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve, so a posterior-cord lesion can paralyze it and weaken shoulder abduction. Brachialis is supplied mainly by the musculocutaneous nerve; flexor digitorum superficialis and pronator teres are supplied by the median nerve. Rhomboids receive the dorsal scapular nerve directly from the C5 root, before the cords form.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: brachialis is supplied mainly by the musculocutaneous nerve, a terminal branch of the lateral cord.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve, which arises from the posterior cord.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: flexor digitorum superficialis is supplied by the median nerve, derived from the medial and lateral cords.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: pronator teres is supplied by the median nerve, not a posterior-cord branch.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: rhomboids are supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve, which branches from the C5 root proximal to the trunks and cords.

A.summary: Brachialis is an anterior-arm flexor supplied primarily by the musculocutaneous nerve; this nerve comes from the lateral cord.

B.summary: The posterior cord gives rise to the axillary nerve, which supplies deltoid; deltoid is a major shoulder abductor.

C.summary: Flexor digitorum superficialis is a median-nerve forearm flexor, not a posterior-cord muscle.

D.summary: Pronator teres is supplied by the median nerve and pronates the forearm.

E.summary: Rhomboids are supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve, which arises directly from the C5 root before the brachial plexus cords.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's brachial plexus diagram traces the posterior cord to the axillary and radial nerves; the axillary nerve supplies the deltoid.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 17-year-old girl who plays soccer is brought to the emergency department after a posterior dislocation of her right knee during a game. The knee is swollen and bruised posteriorly. The dislocation is reduced, but distal pulses are difficult to palpate. Angiograms of the lower extremities are shown. Which vascular structure, indicated by the arrows, is most likely injured?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The popliteal artery lies immediately posterior to the knee joint and is tethered as it passes through the popliteal fossa. Posterior knee dislocation can stretch or tear it, threatening distal limb perfusion; absent or weak pulses require urgent vascular assessment. The angiographic arrows identify the vessel at the knee. The anterior and posterior tibial and fibular arteries are distal branches, while the femoral artery becomes the popliteal artery after passing through the adductor hiatus.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the anterior tibial artery branches from the popliteal artery and travels into the anterior compartment of the leg; it is distal to the knee joint.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the fibular artery is a branch of the posterior tibial artery in the leg, distal to the knee.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: the popliteal artery is the major vessel directly behind the knee and is vulnerable in knee dislocation.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the posterior tibial artery is a distal branch in the posterior leg, below the popliteal fossa.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the femoral artery is proximal to the knee; after traversing the adductor hiatus it is called the popliteal artery.

A.summary: The anterior tibial artery is a distal branch supplying the anterior leg and dorsum of the foot; it is not the artery immediately posterior to the knee.

B.summary: The fibular (peroneal) artery is a branch of the posterior tibial artery in the leg, distal to the popliteal fossa.

C.summary: First Aid identifies the popliteal artery in the popliteal fossa; it continues from the femoral artery and is closely associated with the tibial nerve.

D.summary: The posterior tibial artery travels behind the medial malleolus; it is a distal leg artery rather than the vessel at the knee.

E.summary: The femoral artery passes through the adductor hiatus and continues as the popliteal artery in the popliteal fossa.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's neurovascular-pairing table identifies the popliteal artery in the popliteal fossa (p. 458); the lower-limb arterial diagram shows the distal branches (p. 457).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 54-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit with sepsis secondary to a urinary tract infection. A central venous catheter is to be placed in the right internal jugular vein to monitor hemodynamic information. During the ultrasound-guided procedure, the resident inadvertently pierces the vein and damages structures posterior to the carotid sheath. Which finding is most likely?

options.text: Inability to abduct the right eye
Inability to close the right eye
Paralysis of the platysma on the right

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The cervical sympathetic trunk lies posterior to the carotid sheath. Injury interrupts sympathetic input to the ipsilateral dilator pupillae, producing miosis (pupil constriction), along with possible mild ptosis and anhidrosis: Horner syndrome. The pupillary sphincter remains parasympathetically innervated, so loss of sympathetic dilation leaves the pupil constricted.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: interruption of sympathetic fibers to the dilator pupillae causes ipsilateral miosis.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: mydriasis can result from loss of parasympathetic constrictor input or increased sympathetic drive, not sympathetic-chain injury.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: impaired eye abduction indicates an abducens nerve (CN VI) lesion; CN VI is not the structure posterior to the carotid sheath here.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: eyelid closure is performed by orbicularis oculi, supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII).
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: platysma is supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), not cervical sympathetic fibers.

A.summary: Horner syndrome from sympathetic denervation causes ipsilateral miosis, mild ptosis, and anhidrosis; the pupil constricts because dilator pupillae sympathetic input is lost.

B.summary: Pupillary dilation is mediated by sympathetic activation of dilator pupillae; loss of this pathway causes miosis, not mydriasis.

C.summary: CN VI innervates lateral rectus; a lesion causes inability to abduct the eye and is anatomically distinct from the cervical sympathetic trunk.

D.summary: CN VII supplies orbicularis oculi, which closes the eyelids.

E.summary: CN VII supplies platysma, a superficial muscle of facial expression in the neck.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's Horner syndrome diagram and summary describe sympathetic-chain injury causing ipsilateral miosis, ptosis, and anhidrosis (p. 555).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 58-year-old man is brought to his physician by family members because of recent cognitive changes. His family is concerned that he can no longer recognize common objects in his surroundings. Neurologic examination shows that when he is presented with a picture of a dog, he can copy the picture but cannot recognize the animal as a dog. This finding is most likely caused by a lesion in which area?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is visual agnosia: the patient can see and copy an object but cannot identify it. Visual information reaches primary visual cortex and is then interpreted by visual association cortex. The ventral occipitotemporal (“what”) pathway supports recognition of objects, faces, and other visual content; a lesion in temporo-occipital association cortex can cause visual agnosia. The preserved ability to copy argues against a primary visual or motor deficit.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the angular gyrus participates in language-related integration, including reading and writing functions.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the frontal eye field controls voluntary conjugate gaze, especially contralateral horizontal gaze.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: parieto-occipital association cortex is associated with spatial attention and integration, not the classic ventral-stream object-recognition deficit described.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the precentral gyrus is primary motor cortex; a lesion causes contralateral motor weakness.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: prefrontal cortex supports executive function, planning, and behavior rather than visual object identification.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: the ventral temporo-occipital association pathway processes visual identity (“what”), and injury can cause visual agnosia.

A.summary: The angular gyrus is part of the association cortex involved in language and symbolic processing; it is not the primary visual object-recognition area.

B.summary: The frontal eye field coordinates voluntary contralateral horizontal gaze.

C.summary: Parietal association regions contribute to spatial attention; the ventral visual stream is the pathway for object identity.

D.summary: The precentral gyrus is primary motor cortex and controls voluntary movement.

E.summary: Prefrontal cortex is involved in executive function, planning, and behavior.

F.summary: The temporo-occipital association cortex is part of the ventral “what” pathway and supports recognition of visual objects.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's cerebral-cortex diagram places visual association cortex in the occipitotemporal region; the ventral “what” pathway supports object recognition (p. 512).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A newborn is delivered at 43 weeks' gestation after a difficult breech delivery. The infant's arm was extended overhead to free the impacted head. After delivery, the arm is adducted and internally rotated, with an extended elbow and pronated forearm. Radiographs show no abnormalities. Loss of innervation to which muscle best accounts for the extended elbow and pronated forearm?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is Erb palsy from traction injury to the upper trunk (C5-C6) of the brachial plexus during a difficult delivery. The classic arm posture reflects loss of shoulder abduction/external rotation and elbow flexion/supination. The biceps brachii is especially important because it both flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; denervation leaves the elbow extended and forearm pronated.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: biceps brachii (musculocutaneous nerve, C5-C6) flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; its loss explains both findings.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: brachialis flexes the elbow but does not supinate the forearm; biceps loss best accounts for the combined posture.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: coracobrachialis flexes and adducts the shoulder, not the elbow or forearm.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: deltoid abducts the shoulder and is supplied by the axillary nerve; it does not flex the elbow or supinate the forearm.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: pronator teres pronates the forearm; loss would reduce pronation rather than produce a pronated posture.

A.summary: Upper-trunk C5-C6 injury (Erb palsy) can weaken the musculocutaneous nerve; biceps brachii flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm.

B.summary: Brachialis is an elbow flexor supplied primarily by the musculocutaneous nerve; it does not supinate the forearm.

C.summary: Coracobrachialis acts at the shoulder, flexing and adducting the arm.

D.summary: Deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve and abducts the arm at the shoulder.

E.summary: Pronator teres is a median-nerve muscle that pronates the forearm.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's brachial-plexus lesion figure identifies Erb palsy from C5-C6 upper-trunk traction (p. 452); upper-extremity nerve/muscle tables connect musculocutaneous injury to elbow-flexion and supination weakness (p. 450).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 46-year-old woman with a history of Lyme disease undergoes excision of a right Baker cyst. Three months later, she has decreased sensation over the dorsum of the foot, especially in the web space between the first and second toes. She trips while walking and has mild right foot drop. Dysfunction of which muscle most likely causes her motor symptoms?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: Excision of a Baker cyst can injure or scar the common fibular nerve as it courses through the popliteal fossa. Its deep branch supplies the anterior leg compartment, including tibialis anterior, which dorsiflexes the ankle. Weak dorsiflexion causes foot drop and toe-catching; sensory loss in the first dorsal web space specifically points to the deep fibular nerve. The other listed muscles do not dorsiflex the ankle.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: flexor hallucis longus is a posterior-compartment muscle supplied by the tibial nerve; it flexes the great toe and assists plantar flexion.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: fibularis brevis is supplied by the superficial fibular nerve and everts the foot; it does not dorsiflex it.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: fibularis longus is also a superficial-fibular-nerve muscle that everts and plantar-flexes the foot.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: tibialis anterior is supplied by the deep fibular nerve and is a primary ankle dorsiflexor.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: tibialis posterior is supplied by the tibial nerve and primarily inverts and plantar-flexes the foot.

A.summary: Tibial-nerve posterior-compartment muscles include the toe flexors; flexor hallucis longus flexes the great toe and assists plantar flexion.

B.summary: The superficial fibular nerve supplies the lateral-compartment fibularis muscles, which evert the foot.

C.summary: Fibularis longus is a lateral-compartment muscle supplied by the superficial fibular nerve; it everts the foot.

D.summary: The common fibular nerve divides into superficial and deep branches. Deep fibular injury weakens anterior-compartment dorsiflexion and can produce foot drop; the first web space is its sensory territory.

E.summary: Tibial-nerve posterior-compartment muscles include tibialis posterior, which inverts and plantar-flexes the foot.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid 2026's lower-extremity nerve table links common fibular nerve injury, including compression by a Baker cyst, with dorsal-foot sensory loss and foot drop; the deep fibular branch supplies the anterior compartment (printed p. 457).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 35-year-old man sustains a humeral fracture during a rugby game. Two months later, he has difficulty abducting the arm, especially beyond the first 15 degrees, and decreased sensation over the lateral shoulder. Where is the fracture most likely located?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: This is an axillary nerve lesion. The nerve wraps around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid and teres minor, as well as skin over the lateral shoulder. The supraspinatus initiates the first 15 degrees of abduction; the deltoid abducts the arm thereafter, explaining the deficit beyond 15 degrees. A midshaft fracture more typically injures the radial nerve and causes wrist/finger extension weakness.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the anatomical neck is within the shoulder-joint capsule; it is not the characteristic site for axillary nerve injury.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: a lateral epicondyle fracture can affect structures near the elbow, not the axillary nerve or lateral shoulder sensation.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: a medial epicondyle fracture may injure the ulnar nerve and cause medial-hand symptoms.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: a midshaft humeral fracture can injure the radial nerve, causing wrist drop and posterior-limb sensory loss.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the axillary nerve passes around the surgical neck; injury weakens deltoid-mediated abduction and reduces lateral-shoulder sensation.

A.summary: First Aid describes axillary nerve injury after shoulder dislocation or surgical-neck fracture, rather than an isolated anatomical-neck fracture.

B.summary: Distal humeral injuries are associated with forearm/hand nerve findings; they do not match the axillary nerve's lateral-shoulder territory.

C.summary: Medial epicondyle fracture can injure the ulnar nerve and affect intrinsic hand function and ulnar-digit sensation.

D.summary: A humeral midshaft fracture is associated with radial nerve injury and wrist drop.

E.summary: Axillary nerve injury at the surgical neck causes deltoid weakness, loss of arm abduction beyond 15 degrees, and lateral-arm sensory loss.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid's upper-extremity nerve table associates a humeral surgical-neck fracture with axillary nerve injury, flattened deltoid, impaired abduction beyond 15 degrees, and lateral-arm sensory loss (printed p. 450).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 55-year-old woman with depression is admitted after deep lacerations of the distal wrist and palm. Several weeks later, she has hand weakness and numbness with flattening of the thenar eminence. Which additional finding is most likely?

options.text: Loss of sensation over the palmar aspect of the fifth digit
Weakness of the first and second lumbricals

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: Flattening of the thenar eminence after a distal wrist/palm laceration indicates injury to the median nerve or its recurrent motor branch. The median nerve supplies the first and second lumbricals and thenar muscles. Pronation is mediated by forearm muscles proximal to the wrist and should be spared by a distal lesion. Fifth-digit sensation and thumb adduction are ulnar-nerve functions; thumb extension is radial-nerve mediated.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: palmar sensation over the fifth digit is supplied by the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: pronation is produced by pronator teres and pronator quadratus in the forearm, proximal to the wrist laceration.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: thumb adduction is primarily performed by adductor pollicis, supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: thumb extension is performed by radial-nerve-innervated posterior forearm muscles.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the first and second lumbricals are median-nerve supplied and may be weakened by a distal median-nerve injury.

A.summary: The ulnar nerve supplies sensation to the medial 1½ digits, including the fifth digit.

B.summary: Median-nerve forearm branches supply pronator teres and pronator quadratus; a distal wrist lesion occurs after these branches.

C.summary: Adductor pollicis is an ulnar-nerve muscle; First Aid distinguishes it from the median-innervated thenar group.

D.summary: Radial-nerve branches supply the posterior forearm extensors, including muscles that extend the thumb.

E.summary: First Aid assigns the first and second lumbricals to the median nerve; lumbricals flex MCP and extend IP joints.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid's hand-muscle table identifies the first two lumbricals and most thenar muscles as median-nerve supplied; distal median injury produces thenar weakness/atrophy, whereas ulnar muscles control thumb adduction (printed p. 452).
